checks.message: Image scanning on push not enabled
checks.context: Without scan-on-push, vulnerable base images silently accumulate in your registry. A single compromised container image can give an attacker a foothold in every environment it's deployed to.

checks.message: ECR repository encryption not explicitly configured
checks.context: By default ECR uses AES-256 managed by AWS. Specifying KMS gives you an audit trail of every image pull via CloudTrail and the ability to revoke access by disabling the key.

checks.message: Review repository policy for wildcard principals
checks.context: A repository policy with Principal:* allows any AWS account to pull images. This can expose proprietary code or be used to distribute malicious images. Scope access to specific account IDs or IAM roles.

checks.message: Repository deletion removes all images permanently
checks.context: Deleting an ECR repository destroys all container images and tags. Any ECS tasks, EKS pods, or Lambda functions referencing images in this repository will fail to pull on next deployment.
Deleted images cannot be recovered. Ensure no running workloads depend on the images being deleted, and that you are not deleting the only copy of a production image.

checks.message: Enable Container Insights for this cluster
checks.context: Without Container Insights you have no visibility into container-level CPU, memory, or network anomalies — making it very hard to detect a compromised container or a cryptominer running in your cluster.

checks.message: Verify task definition does not use privileged containers
checks.context: A privileged ECS container has root access to the underlying host. If compromised, an attacker can escape the container and access every other task on the same EC2 instance, including their credentials.

checks.message: Ensure the task role follows least-privilege
checks.context: ECS task roles are attached to every container in the service. Overly permissive task roles mean a compromised container can access AWS services far beyond what the application needs.

checks.message: Verify the new task definition does not introduce privileged containers or excessive permissions
checks.context: Service updates deploy new task definitions to running containers. A malicious or misconfigured task definition update can compromise the entire service.

checks.message: Service deletion will terminate all running tasks
checks.context: Deleting an ECS service stops all running tasks immediately. If the service handles live traffic, this causes an outage. Use --force only when you are certain the service should be stopped.

checks.message: Container agent update may briefly interrupt task placement on this instance
checks.context: During the update, the agent restarts and the instance temporarily stops accepting new task placements. Existing running tasks are not affected, but ensure other instances can handle the load.
